headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared filesystem and code-execution defaults; no critical interaction is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read and write working directories and execute tool calls/code, while Mentat reads files passed on the command line and writes filesystem diffs. If AutoGen places attacker-controlled content into shared files, Mentat may treat it as trusted input. The pair has a filesystem bridge, so injection is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory
IF AutoGen writes untrusted content into files that Mentat later reads
mitigations: Use separate working directories for each agent
Require manual review of any file Mentat reads from AutoGen outputs
Prefix AutoGen-generated artifacts with a non-executable marker convention
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files into prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read filesystem content and send prompts to configured model providers, and both touch user-provided application/source-code data. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose the other's files or derived context to external inference backends. The blast radius includes source code and application data, so this is more than low risk.
conditions: IF the two agents share a workspace containing sensitive source code or application data
IF either agent forwards file contents or derived context to its configured model provider
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Restrict each agent to least-privilege file subsets
Review provider logging and retention settings before use
Avoid placing secrets in files accessible to both agents
requires-engineering: add redaction before model-provider calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has unrestricted filesystem write and subprocess execution, while Mentat has filesystem write plus git-state modification. Their shared-state model is filesystem-based for Mentat and developer-defined for AutoGen, so concurrent edits can collide on the same files or repository state. This is a real default-path conflict even though AutoGen does not itself modify git state.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF AutoGen subprocesses or file writes overlap with Mentat git edits
mitigations: Serialize access to the shared repository
Assign disjoint file subsets to each agent
Pause one agent while the other commits or rewrites files
Use separate branches for each agent's changes
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code, plans, or facts that Mentat may then turn into diffs or edits. Mentat's diff-based workflow and multi-file editing make it likely to act on upstream output unless a human verifies it. That creates a default cascade from one agent's output into the other's actions, though not an irreversible one by itself.
conditions: IF Mentat applies edits derived from AutoGen output without independent verification
IF AutoGen's generated instructions are treated as authoritative
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents
Ask Mentat to restate assumptions before editing
Compare proposed diffs against source-of-truth files
Limit AutoGen to drafting only, not final instructions
requires-engineering: add automated verification of upstream claims

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and describe general code/application data handling, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. The only concrete compliance concern is that both can handle provider API keys and user data, but the profiles do not show a specific regulatory conflict. The other agent is cited because the assessment is pairwise, though no mismatch is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent without a matching policy
IF provider logging/retention settings are not reviewed
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Confirm provider retention settings before use
Document data-handling boundaries for each agent
Use separate accounts for sensitive and non-sensitive work
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement
